examples.ko: 사고가 나서 경찰이 교통정리를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: There was an accident, so the police are directing traffic.

examples.ko: 퇴근 시간에는 차가 많아서 교통정리가 필요해요.
examples.en: During rush hour there are many cars, so traffic control is needed.
A man helped direct traffic in front of the construction site.

examples.ko: 이 사거리는 교통정리가 잘 안 돼서 늘 복잡해요.
examples.en: Traffic isn't managed well at this intersection, so it's always chaotic.
On festival days, volunteers take charge of directing traffic.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오는 날에는 교통정리 인원이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: On days with heavy rain, more people are needed to direct traffic.

explain: 길에서 차와 사람이 잘 다니도록 신호를 보내 주는 일을 말해요. 경찰이나 도우미가 손짓으로 하는 모습이 먼저 떠올라요. 복잡한 일이나 의견을 정리할 때도 비유로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 의견이 너무 많아서 팀장님이 교통정리를 했어요.
phrases.en: There were too many opinions, so the team leader sorted things out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복잡하게 얽힌 의견이나 일을 한 번에 정리해 주는 것을 말해요. 회사나 모임에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means sorting out tangled opinions or tasks in one go. You often hear it at work or in meetings.
phrases.en_equiv: sort things out; untangle the mess

explain_en: It refers to guiding cars and people with signals so they can move smoothly, like a police officer waving traffic through. People also use it figuratively for sorting out a messy situation or many opinions.

examples.en: During holidays, the highways turn into traffic hell.
I leave early to avoid the commuting traffic hell.
When it rains, Seoul turns into a traffic nightmare.
Every holiday, we go through the traffic hell of heading home.
This city is a traffic nightmare morning and evening.

examples.ko: 교통지옥 때문에 회사에 한 시간이나 늦었어요.
examples.en: Because of the terrible traffic, I was an hour late to work.

explain: 차가 너무 막혀서 꼼짝 못 하는 상황을 과장해서 말하는 표현이에요. 뉴스나 일상 대화에서 '교통지옥에 갇히다', '교통지옥이 따로 없다'처럼 자주 써요. 그냥 '차가 막히다'보다 힘든 감정이 더 커요.
explain_en: It exaggerates a situation where traffic is so bad you can't move. You hear it in the news and daily talk, as in '교통지옥에 갇히다'. It carries more frustration than simply saying '차가 막히다'.

examples.ko: 교통질서를 잘 지켜야 사고가 안 나요.
examples.en: You have to follow traffic rules well to avoid accidents.
They teach children about traffic rules in front of the school.

examples.ko: 모두가 교통질서를 지키면 길이 덜 막혀요.
examples.en: If everyone obeys traffic rules, the roads are less congested.
Traffic is so disorderly that walking feels scary.
They guide foreign tourists on traffic rules too.
A traffic order campaign was held this morning.

explain: 신호를 지키고 차선을 지키는 것처럼 길에서 모두가 따르는 약속을 말해요. '교통질서를 지키다'가 가장 자주 쓰이고, 어기면 '교통질서를 어지럽히다'라고 해요. '교통법규'는 법으로 정한 규칙이고, '교통질서'는 그 규칙을 지키는 길 위의 질서 상태를 말해요.
explain_en: It means the shared rules everyone follows on the road, like obeying signals and lanes. The most common pairing is '교통질서를 지키다', and breaking them is '교통질서를 어지럽히다'. '교통법규' are the rules set by law, while '교통질서' is the orderly state on the road when those rules are followed.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 구급약을 꼭 챙겨요.
examples.en: I always pack first-aid medicine when I travel.

examples.ko: 집에 구급약이 하나도 없어서 약국에 갔어요.
examples.en: We had no first-aid medicine at home, so I went to the pharmacy.
The first-aid kit is in the living room drawer.
Basic first-aid medicine is available at the campsite.

examples.ko: 유효 기간이 지난 구급약은 버려야 해요.
examples.en: You should throw away first-aid medicine that has expired.

examples.ko: 아이가 다쳐서 구급약으로 응급 처치를 했어요.
examples.en: The child got hurt, so I gave first aid with the medicine from the kit.

explain: 밴드, 소독약, 연고, 소화제처럼 갑자기 아플 때 쓰려고 미리 준비해 두는 약이에요. 집에서는 '비상약'이나 '상비약'이라고도 많이 말해요. '구급약 상자'는 '구급상자'라고도 해요.
explain_en: These are things like bandages, antiseptic, ointment and digestive medicine kept ready for sudden needs. At home, people also say '비상약' or '상비약'. A 'first-aid box' can be '구급약 상자' or '구급상자'.

examples.ko: 옷에 구김이 많이 가서 다림질해야 해요.
examples.en: My clothes are very wrinkled, so I need to iron them.

examples.ko: 이 셔츠는 구김이 잘 안 생겨요.
examples.en: This shirt doesn't wrinkle easily.

examples.ko: 구김 없이 옷을 펴서 걸어 두세요.
examples.en: Please spread out the clothes and hang them without creases.
I put the skirt in my bag and it got creased.
I tried smoothing out the creases in the paper with my hand.
I sprayed anti-wrinkle spray on my clothes.

explain: 옷이나 종이가 접히거나 눌려서 생긴 자국이에요. 얼굴이나 피부의 주름은 '주름'이라고 해서 구별해요. '구김이 가다', '구김이 생기다'로 자주 말하고, 구김을 만드는 동작은 '구기다'예요.
explain_en: This is the mark left when cloth or paper is folded or pressed. For wrinkles on the face or skin, use '주름' instead. It pairs with '구김이 가다/생기다', and the action of creasing is '구기다'.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 구김살 없이 밝게 자랐어요.
examples.en: That child grew up bright and carefree.
I smoothed the wrinkles out of my clothes with an iron.
I like her carefree smile.

examples.ko: 빨래를 널 때 구김살을 손으로 털어요.
examples.en: When hanging laundry, I shake out the wrinkles by hand.
Maybe because of worry, his face looked creased and tense.

examples.ko: 구김살 하나 없는 새 교복을 입었어요.
examples.en: I wore a brand-new school uniform without a single wrinkle.

explain: '구김'과 거의 같은 뜻이지만, '구김살 없다'처럼 마음이나 표정이 밝고 어두운 그늘이 없다는 뜻으로 더 자주 써요. 옷의 주름에는 '구김'이 더 일상적이에요.

phrases.example: 구김살 없이 자란 아이라서 누구한테나 친절해요.
phrases.en: He grew up carefree, so he's kind to everyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려움이나 그늘 없이 밝고 자유롭게 자란 사람이나 표정을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It praises a person or expression that is bright and free of worry or hardship.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '구김', but it is more often used in '구김살 없다' to describe a bright mind or face with no shadow. For clothes, '구김' sounds more everyday.

examples.ko: 학술지 구독료가 비싸서 학교 도서관을 통해 읽어요.
examples.en: The journal subscription fee is expensive, so I read it through the school library.
The newspaper subscription fee went up again.

examples.ko: 월 구독료를 내면 영화를 무제한으로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pay a monthly subscription fee, you can watch unlimited movies.
I set the subscription fee to be paid automatically by card.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 구독료 없이 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this app without a subscription fee.
The subscription fee was a burden, so I cancelled the service.

explain: 신문, 잡지뿐 아니라 요즘은 음악, 영상, 앱 서비스에 내는 정기 요금도 구독료라고 해요. '월 구독료', '구독료를 내다'처럼 써요. 서비스를 그만두는 건 '구독을 해지하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Besides newspapers and magazines, it now also covers regular fees for music, video and app services. You say '월 구독료' and '구독료를 내다'. Quitting a service is '구독을 해지하다'.

examples.en: The toes of my shoes were scuffed, so I applied shoe polish.
There's dust on the toes of my shoes.
The toes of my shoes got soaked because of the rain.
Shoes with pointed toes hurt my feet.
I tripped on the threshold and scuffed the toe of my shoe.
Before the interview, I polished my shoe toes until they shone.

explain: 구두의 앞쪽 끝부분을 말해요. 운동화에는 보통 '신발 앞코'라고 해요. '구두코가 닳다', '구두코가 뾰족하다'처럼 모양과 상태를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is the front tip of a dress shoe. For sneakers, people usually say '신발 앞코'. It is used to describe the shape or condition, as in '구두코가 닳다' or '구두코가 뾰족하다'.

examples.en: With a shoehorn, I can put on shoes easily.
I hung a shoehorn at the entrance.
If I put them on without a shoehorn, the heel gets folded.
I got a long shoehorn as a gift.
I put on my sneakers with a shoehorn.
I put a small shoehorn in my travel bag too.

explain: 뒤꿈치가 잘 들어가도록 신발 뒤에 대고 쓰는 도구예요. 쓸 때는 '구둣주걱으로 신다'처럼 말해요. 발음할 때 '구두쭈걱'으로 소리 나는 점을 기억하세요.
explain_en: It is a tool placed behind the heel so your foot slides into the shoe. You say '구둣주걱으로 신다'. Remember that it is pronounced '구두쭈걱'.

examples.en: If you cross the overpass, the subway station is right there.

examples.ko: 이 구름다리는 큰 도로 위에 있어요.
examples.en: This overpass is above a big road.
The night view from the overpass is wonderful.
I held my child's hand and crossed the overpass.
A new overpass was built between the parks.
The overpass stairs are high, so it's tiring.

explain: 도로나 철길 위로 사람이 걸어서 건너는 높은 다리예요. '육교'라고도 해요. 건물과 건물 사이를 잇는 다리를 말할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is an elevated bridge people walk across over a road or railway, also called '육교'. It can also describe a bridge connecting two buildings.

examples.en: There's a stink coming from the shoe cabinet.
The stink from the drain made me open the window.
I sprayed air freshener to get rid of the stink.
The old cheese gave off a terrible stink.
I don't know where the stink is coming from.
The sweaty socks gave off a stink.

explain: 똥이나 썩은 것, 오래된 신발과 양말처럼 코를 찌르는 안 좋은 냄새예요. '고린내'는 비슷하지만 느낌이 조금 작은 말이에요. '냄새가 나다'보다 더 불쾌한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Something about this contract smells fishy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로는 괜찮아 보여도 뭔가 수상하고 떳떳하지 못한 느낌이 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is used when something seems suspicious or shady even though it looks fine on the surface.

explain_en: This is a nasty smell like feces, rotten things, or old shoes and socks. '고린내' is a similar word with a slightly smaller feel. It feels more unpleasant than just '냄새가 나다'.

examples.ko: 휴가 때 햇볕에 타서 피부가 구릿빛이 됐어요.
examples.en: I got tanned in the sun on vacation and my skin turned bronze.
Bronzed skin looks healthy.
That athlete's bronzed forearms look great.
I walked through the autumn fields tinted copper.
The old statue has a copper hue.
I saw a bronze-skinned surfer on the beach.

explain: 구리처럼 붉은 갈색을 띠는 색이에요. 햇볕에 보기 좋게 탄 피부를 말할 때 가장 자주 나오고, 보통 건강하고 멋진 느낌이에요. 사이시옷 때문에 '구리삗'으로 소리 나요.
explain_en: It is the reddish brown of copper. It most often describes skin nicely tanned by the sun, usually with a healthy, attractive feel. Because of the 사이시옷, it is pronounced '구리삗'.

examples.en: The road winds on and on.
We climbed up the winding mountain path.
The river winds through the fields.
My hair is wavy, so I straighten it every day.
I got lost in the winding alleys.
The snake slithered away in curves.

explain: 길, 강, 머리카락처럼 길쭉한 것이 이리저리 굽은 모양이에요. '구불구불하다'로도 쓰고, 길이 꼬불꼬불한 건 '꼬불꼬불'이 더 작고 촘촘한 느낌이에요. 곧은 모양은 '쭉' 또는 '똑바로'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes long things like roads, rivers and hair bending this way and that. It also works as '구불구불하다'. '꼬불꼬불' feels smaller and tighter, while straight shapes are '쭉' or '똑바로'.

examples.en: I feel comfortable sitting in a secluded seat.

examples.ko: 식당 가장 구석진 곳에 자리를 잡았어요.
examples.en: We took a seat in the most tucked-away corner of the restaurant.
There is a small shop in a hidden alley.

examples.ko: 이 방은 너무 구석져서 햇빛이 안 들어요.
examples.en: This room is so tucked away that no sunlight comes in.
It's hard to clean even the out-of-the-way corners.

examples.ko: 구석져 보이지만 가 보면 분위기가 좋아요.
examples.en: It looks out of the way, but the atmosphere is nice once you go.

explain: 주로 '구석진 곳, 구석진 자리'처럼 꾸미는 형태로 나와요. 사람들 눈에 잘 안 띄는 안쪽이나 모퉁이를 말해서 아늑할 수도, 쓸쓸할 수도 있어요. 멀리 떨어진 시골에는 '외지다'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in the modifying form, like '구석진 곳' or '구석진 자리'. It points to an inner spot or corner people don't easily notice, which can feel cozy or lonely. For remote countryside places, '외지다' fits better.

examples.en: The smell is so bad that I feel nauseous.
I rode in the car for a long time and now I feel nauseous.

examples.ko: 그 장면을 보고 구역질이 날 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I felt like gagging when I saw that scene.
I opened the window to hold back the nausea.

examples.ko: 이틀 전부터 구역질이 나고 입맛이 없어요.
examples.en: Since two days ago, I've felt nauseous and have had no appetite.
After taking the medicine, the nausea stopped.

explain: 토할 것처럼 속이 울렁거리고 헛구역질이 나는 느낌이에요. 실제로 토하는 건 '토하다'이고, '속이 안 좋다'나 '메스껍다'는 더 부드러운 말이에요. 아주 싫은 것을 보았을 때도 '구역질이 나다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of your stomach heaving as if you will vomit. Actually throwing up is '토하다', while '속이 안 좋다' and '메스껍다' are softer. People also say '구역질이 나다' when they find something disgusting.

examples.en: The rescue workers were given the task of finding missing people.
A rescue worker helped a hiker who was hurt on the mountain.
The 119 rescue workers arrived quickly.
To become a rescue worker, you need to be physically strong.

examples.ko: 홍수 때 구조대원들이 주민을 보트로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: During the flood, rescue workers moved residents by boat.
My father has worked as a rescue worker for ten years.

explain: 사고나 재난 현장에서 위험한 사람을 구하는 사람이에요. 불을 끄는 사람은 '소방관'이라고 하고, 구조 일을 전문으로 맡는 팀은 '구조대'라고 해요. 높여 말할 때는 '구조대원분'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is a person who saves people in danger at accidents or disasters. People who fight fires are '소방관', and the team specializing in rescue is '구조대'. To be polite, say '구조대원분'.

examples.ko: 정부는 피해 지역에 구호품을 신속히 보내겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The government said it would quickly send relief supplies to the affected area.
Our class packed boxes of relief supplies.
When the relief supplies arrived, the residents lined up.
Relief supplies like blankets and bottled water are needed.
We loaded the relief supplies collected by citizens onto a truck.

examples.ko: 구호품 배송이 길 때문에 늦어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The delivery of relief supplies is delayed because of the roads.

explain: 재난이나 가난으로 힘든 사람들에게 보내는 물건이에요. 돈은 '성금'이나 '기부금', 물건은 '구호품'이라고 구별해요. 뉴스에서 '구호품을 전달하다', '구호품을 지급하다'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: These are goods sent to people suffering from disaster or poverty. Money is '성금' or '기부금', while goods are '구호품'. In the news you often see '구호품을 전달하다' and '구호품을 지급하다'.

examples.en: This bridge construction is a major national project.
National projects cost a lot of tax money.
They decided to build a new airport as a national project.
He has experience taking part in a national project.

examples.ko: 국가사업이라서 일정을 마음대로 바꿀 수 없어요.
examples.en: Because it's a national project, we can't change the schedule as we like.
I saw the national projects the government is pushing on the news.

explain: 도로, 공항, 연구처럼 나라가 계획하고 돈을 들여 하는 큰 일이에요. 보통 '국가사업으로 추진하다', '국가사업을 벌이다'처럼 뉴스나 기사에서 많이 나와요. 회사가 하는 일은 그냥 '사업'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a big undertaking planned and funded by the nation, such as roads, airports or research. It often appears in the news as '국가사업으로 추진하다'. What companies do is simply '사업'.

examples.en: This meat is domestic, so I eat it with confidence.
Domestic fruit is more expensive than imported fruit.
At the mart, I only pick domestically grown beans.
The label says it is domestic.
Domestic and imported products taste very different.
This is kimchi made only with domestic ingredients.

explain: 주로 식재료나 농산물이 우리나라에서 나거나 만들어졌다는 뜻으로 마트 표시에 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '수입산'이에요. 공장 제품에는 '국산'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is common on supermarket labels to say that food or produce comes from Korea. The opposite is '수입산'. For factory-made goods, '국산' sounds more natural.

examples.en: National character differs a little from country to country.

examples.ko: 한국 사람의 국민성을 한마디로 말하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to describe Korean national character in one word.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 영국의 국민성을 잘 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows British national character well.

examples.ko: 국민성은 역사와 환경의 영향을 받는다고 해요.
examples.en: They say national character is influenced by history and environment.
While traveling, I felt the national character of that country.

examples.ko: 국민성을 단정해서 말하는 것은 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should be careful about making definite claims about national character.

explain: 한 나라 사람들에게 두루 나타난다고 여겨지는 성격이나 태도를 말해요. '한국 사람은 빨리빨리 한다'처럼 흔히 하는 이야기가 여기에 들어가요. '민족성'과 비슷하지만 '국민성'은 민족이 아니라 나라를 기준으로 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to traits or attitudes thought to be common among a country's people, like 'Koreans do things quickly'. It is similar to '민족성', but '국민성' is based on the nation rather than the ethnic group.

examples.en: The government decided to increase next year's defense spending.
I saw on the news how much the defense spending is.
The debate dragged on because of the defense budget.
The scale of defense spending differs from country to country.
Most of the money spent on defense is tax money.
Voices demanding cuts in defense spending are loud.

explain: 나라를 지키는 일에 쓰는 돈이에요. 뉴스에서 '국방비를 늘리다/줄이다', '국방비 증가'처럼 예산 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '국방 예산'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the money spent on defending the country. In the news it appears in budget talk, such as '국방비를 늘리다/줄이다' and '국방비 증가'. A similar phrase is '국방 예산'.

examples.en: These days, domestic products are of very good quality too.
My grandmother tries to use only domestic products.
There's a poster urging people to use domestic products.
Domestic products are cheaper than foreign ones.
This shop specializes in domestic products.
I chose a domestic product as a gift.

explain: 우리나라에서 만든 물건을 말하고, 반대말은 '수입품'이에요. '국산품 애용'은 오래전부터 쓰던 표어 같은 말이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '국산'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means goods made in Korea, and the opposite is '수입품'. '국산품 애용' is a long-used slogan-like phrase. In daily talk people often just say '국산'.

examples.en: I look up words I don't know in a Korean dictionary.
I bought a Korean dictionary in paper form.
It's not in the Korean dictionary, but everyone uses it.
I often open the Korean dictionary when doing homework.
I installed a Korean dictionary app on my phone.

examples.ko: 이 낱말 뜻은 국어사전에 이렇게 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The meaning of this word is given like this in the Korean dictionary.

explain: 한국 사람이 한국어 낱말의 뜻을 찾는 사전이에요. 학교에서 '국어'는 한국어 과목을 말하기 때문에 '국어사전'이라고 불러요. 요즘은 종이책보다 인터넷 사전이나 앱으로 많이 찾아요.
explain_en: This is the dictionary Koreans use to look up the meaning of Korean words. At school, '국어' is the Korean language subject, hence the name. These days people more often search online or in apps than in paper books.

examples.en: Busan is an international city with a port.
Many foreigners live in this international city.
As an international city, it has restaurants from many countries.
This area was developed as an international city.
My dream is to work in an international city.
To become an international city, transportation must be convenient.

explain: 외국인과 외국 회사가 많고 세계와 활발히 교류하는 도시를 말해요. '국제도시답게', '국제도시로 발전하다'처럼 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '글로벌 도시'도 들려요.
explain_en: It describes a city with many foreigners and foreign companies and active exchange with the world. Common uses are '국제도시답게' and '국제도시로 발전하다'. You may also hear '글로벌 도시'.

examples.en: Our company is trying to internationalize its services.
Universities are internationalizing by teaching classes in English.
It takes time to internationalize the market.
Opinions came up about internationalizing the city.
Sales went up after the brand went international.
If you internationalize a school, the number of international students grows.

explain: 회사, 학교, 도시처럼 하나를 해외 사람들도 이용할 수 있게 바꾼다는 느낌으로 써요. '세계화하다'와 가까워요. 스스로 그렇게 바뀌는 상황에는 '국제화되다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for changing something like a company, school or city so people abroad can also use it. It is close to '세계화하다'. When something changes that way on its own, use '국제화되다'.

examples.en: A chrysanthemum festival is held in autumn.
I placed chrysanthemums in front of my grandmother's photo.
Yellow chrysanthemums have fully bloomed in the yard.
The scent of chrysanthemums fills the room.
I make tea from chrysanthemum flowers and drink it.
I put a bunch of chrysanthemums in a vase.

explain: 가을을 대표하는 꽃이고, 말할 때는 '국화'라고도 해요. 흰 국화는 추모할 때 많이 쓰여서 상황에 따라 분위기가 달라요. 꽃잎으로 만든 '국화차'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a typical autumn flower, also simply called '국화'. White chrysanthemums are often used for mourning, so the mood depends on the setting. There is also '국화차', tea made from the petals.

examples.ko: 저녁 먹기 전에 군것질을 하면 밥맛이 없어요.
examples.en: If I snack before dinner, I lose my appetite.
I bought snacks to nibble on at the cinema.
Children really love snacking.
I gained weight because of snacking.
I keep snacking while studying for exams.
I went to the market to buy some snacks.

explain: 밥 먹는 시간이 아닐 때 과자나 간식을 이것저것 먹는 일이에요. '간식'은 먹는 음식 자체를 가리키지만 '군것질'은 먹는 행동에 가까워요. 먹고 싶어서 자꾸 입에 넣는 느낌이 있어서 '군것질을 끊다', '군것질을 줄이다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means eating snacks here and there outside mealtimes. '간식' can refer to the food itself, while '군것질' is closer to the act of snacking. It carries a feel of nibbling out of habit, as in '군것질을 끊다' and '군것질을 줄이다'.

examples.en: Our team leader assigns work in a military style.
The military-style greeting is so stiff that it's uncomfortable.
Military-style culture has largely disappeared from companies.
Every morning, we line up in military fashion.
Military-style training doesn't suit me.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 군대식 규칙 때문에 말이 많았어요.
examples.en: There was much talk about that school because of its military-style rules.

explain: 군대처럼 명령과 복종이 분명하고 딱딱하게 일하는 방식을 말해요. 좋은 뜻보다는 '너무 엄격하다'는 비판의 느낌으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '군대식 문화', '군대식으로 하다'가 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: It describes a stiff way of working with clear orders and obedience, like the army. It is often used with a critical feel of being too strict. Common uses are '군대식 문화' and '군대식으로 하다'.

examples.en: Since I started exercising, a lot of flab has gone.

examples.ko: 배에 군살이 붙어서 바지가 꽉 껴요.
examples.en: I've got flab on my belly, so my pants are tight.
I envy her lean figure.
I eat a light dinner to lose the flab.
The older you get, the more easily flab builds up.
He has a firm body without an ounce of flab.

explain: 배, 팔뚝, 옆구리처럼 필요 없이 붙은 살을 말해요. 전체 몸무게를 말하는 '살'과 달리 몸의 특정 부분에 붙은 느낌이 강해요. '군살이 붙다/빠지다', '군살이 없다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to unneeded fat on places like the belly, upper arms or sides. Unlike '살', which can be about overall weight, it feels tied to specific body parts. Common uses are '군살이 붙다/빠지다' and '군살이 없다'.

examples.en: The navy school uniform skirt suits you well.
I had a dark navy suit made.
As evening came, the sky turned navy blue.
I mixed navy blue and white to paint.

examples.ko: 군청색 가방이 어떤 옷에나 잘 맞아요.
examples.en: A navy bag goes well with any outfit.

examples.ko: 이 군청색이 제 눈에는 검은색처럼 보여요.
examples.en: To my eyes, this navy looks like black.

explain: 짙고 어두운 파란색이에요. 비슷하게 '남색'이나 '네이비'라고도 말해요. 교복, 양복, 가방처럼 차분한 색을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a deep, dark blue. People also say '남색' or '네이비' for something similar. It fits when describing calm colors of uniforms, suits and bags.
